messages:
jia: Hey - spotted something odd in the canary we rolled at 10:20 UTC. Canary target is 10% but telemetry shows ~0 requests. :eyes:

omar: Huh. Any quick logs or console screenshot?

jia: Screenshot attached in thread (console shows split 90/10). Also saw a bunch of "route=stable (sticky)" lines in the router logs. Snippet of rollout config we used:

```

{
  "traffic_split": [
    { "variant": "stable", "weight": 90, "guard": { "cookie": "session_id" }},
    { "variant": "canary", "weight": 10, "guard": { "header": "X-Client-Attr" }}
  ],
  "sticky": { "by": "cookie", "ttl": 86400 }
}

```

jia: Logs show requests with X-Client-Attr present still being routed to stable with reason=sticky.

vasiliy: My first guess: sticky evaluation probably happens before header guard evaluation. If sticky key only uses session_id, then once a user is sticky to stable they stay regardless of header-based guard.

omar: That would explain zero canary traffic if most active sessions had session_id assigned earlier. Is sticky supposed to be compatible with variant-level guards?

kelsey: From UX side, we expected header guards to override sticky for the canary (we rely on header for targeted A/B). Console rollout UX explicitly mentioned guard precedence but maybe docs are ambiguous.

vasiliy: I quickly grep'd the router code. There's a branch: computeStickyAssignment(); if assigned -> return assignedVariant; else evaluateGuards(). So sticky short-circuits. Looks like expected behavior is configurable but default is sticky-first.

omar: Oof. That's a policy mismatch. Two options: change default to guards-first, or make sticky key composition include the guard header so targeted users remain sticky to canary.

kelsey: Which is less disruptive? Changing default could affect a lot of live rollouts. Adding header into sticky key for variants that declare header guard seems safer and backwards-compatible.

vasiliy: Agreed. Quick patch: when a variant has a guard that references headers, include those header values into the sticky hash. Sketch:

```
// pseudo
stickyKey = session_id
if variant.guard.headers:
  stickyKey += '|' + header_values_joined
assignment = hash(stickyKey) % 100
```

omar: Will that require a migration for existing sticky cookies? They will start having different bucket assignments after change.

vasiliy: Yes - users will re-bucket when key composition changes. TTL might mitigate, but it's a behavior change. We should document it and maybe gate behind a rollout flag for infra teams.

kelsey: For immediate triage — can we set canary weight to 0 in console until we decide? Also add a prominent note in console describing guard vs sticky precedence.

ci-deploy-bot: /deploy rollback canary-1869 -> weight=0 scheduled by @kelsey at 1869002530

sre-bot: Alert created: routing-anomaly-1869002468. Pager notified to eng-runtime.

omar: I'll open an RFC/PR describing both fixes (guard-first vs include-guard-in-sticky) with perf tests. Assigning to vasiliy for prototype change.

vasiliy: Taking it. Will prototype header-in-sticky today, add feature flag, and a unit test matrix covering cookie-only, header-only, and combined.

kelsey: Thanks. Also can we add a small histogram to console telemetry: percent of requests short-circuited by sticky vs evaluated by guard? That will help surface regressions.

omar: Good idea. I'll file a telemetry ticket and ping analytics.

jia: Thanks all — good catch. Leaving the rollback in place for now. Will post repro steps and a minimal log dump in the ticket. :thumbsup:
